Of course, there are reasons for prices going up. AI developers are building giant data centres filled with racks of powerful servers, using many of the same components needed to make devices like the Steam Frame.

Ram prices alone more than doubled in price between October 2025 and the start of 2026 . Meanwhile, the graphics card I bought for £500 a few months ago now sits at closer to £650.

As prices climb higher and higher, hardware developers don't have much of a choice but to put up their own.

"We set out to come out with a device that would have been much more affordable," Valve developer Jeremy Selan said.

"But the global Ram market has impacted us the same way it's impacted everybody."

"The idea that it's too expensive is one of the biggest...
body.zh: Valve 的新款虚拟现实耳机 Steam Frame 已正式发布，但价格高昂。 其硬件非常出色，是一款佩戴舒适、采用巧妙技术的轻便设备，只要您愿意花 1,089 英镑购买一款具有 1TB 存储空间的耳机。 两者都能够从 PC 上进行流媒体播放，也能够在设备上玩游戏，并取得了不同程度的成功。 但它的价格标签会让很多人翻白眼，而且并不能消除人们对日益昂贵的虚拟现实头显让人们放弃这项爱好的批评。 但在我们讨论这个高昂的价格之前，Steam Frame 真的好吗？ 我拥有 VR 耳机已有十多年了，Valve 的最新成果给我留下了美好的第一印象。 游戏运行良好——考虑到价格标签，这确实是最低限度——而且它很容易使用。 优点之一是，与 Meta 的 Quest 3 一样，它具有扁平的“煎饼”镜片，让您戴上耳机时可以清晰地看到。 它很轻——只比一罐汤重一点。但让它感到舒适的是决定将内部结构分开。 电池组位于您的后脑勺上，而屏幕位于前面，这意味着您不会感到前部沉重，这是其他耳机常见的批评。 但还有更好的屏幕。例如，PlayStation VR2 拥有令人难以置信的 OLED 显示屏，尽管没有薄饼镜头。 然而，这些产品的溢价非常高，其成本远远高于 Steam Frame。 当 Meta 于 2023 年 6 月推出 Quest 3 时，其 128GB 型号的零售价为 480 英镑。存储空间更少，但价格却低得多。 三年后，当 Quest 3 感觉像是一个转折点时，很难相信 VR 会变得越来越贵。 “今天的虚拟现实最终是一个高端利基市场，”游戏作家克里斯托弗·德林告诉我。 “Meta 一直在补贴 Quest 硬件，很难想象他们会在放弃这些体验时继续前进。” 当然，价格上涨是有原因的。人工智能开发人员正在建造巨大的数据中心，其中充满了强大服务器的机架，使用许多与制造 Steam Frame 等设备所需的相同组件。 从 2025 年 10 月到 2026 年初，仅公羊的价格就上涨了一倍多。与此同时，我几个月前花 500 英镑购买的显卡现在价格接近 650 英镑。 随着价格越来越高，硬件开发商别无选择，只能自己开发。 Valve 开发者杰里米·塞兰 (Jeremy Selan) 表示：“我们打算推出一款价格更加实惠的设备。” “但全球公羊市场对我们的影响就像对每个人的影响一样。” “价格太贵是最大的想法之一......

reflection.en: The Steam Frame headset is lauded for its excellent technology and comfortable design, but its steep price of £1,089 raises questions about accessibility. This echoes the biblical caution that while knowledge and capability may advance, not everything that can be done is necessarily beneficial or wise for all people.
reflection.zh: Steam Frame头显因其出色的技术和舒适的设计而受到赞扬，但其高达1089英镑的昂贵价格引发了关于可及性的问题。这呼应了圣经中的告诫：虽然知识和能力可能在进步，但并非所有能做到的事情都对所有人有益或明智。

verse.textEn: "I have the right to do anything," you say — but not everything is beneficial. "I have the right to do anything" — but not everything is constructive.
verse.textZh: 凡事都可行，但不都有益处；凡事都可行，但不都造就人。

title.en: What is AI, how does it work and why are some people concerned about it?
title.zh: 人工智能是什么，它是如何工作的，为什么有些人担心它？

summary.en: AI is transforming modern life, but not without worry for some that it may be abused or have an adverse environmental impact.
summary.zh: 人工智能正在改变现代生活，但有些人担心它可能被滥用或对环境产生不利影响。

body.en:
The technology takes many forms - from personalising social media feeds to spotting friends in smartphone photos - and accelerating medical breakthroughs.

But the rise of chatbots like OpenAI's ChatGPT has prompted concern about the tech's environmental impact, ethical implications and data use.

Recent claims that AI could become too powerful and threaten humanity have also triggered calls for slower development and tighter regulation.

AI allows computers to process large amounts of data, identify patterns and follow detailed instructions about what to do with that information.

However, scientists have developed systems that can perform tasks which usually require human intelligence, trying to replicate how people acquire and use knowledge.

This could be trying to anticipate what product an online shopper might buy, based on previous purchases, in order to recommend items.

The technology is also behind voice-controlled virtual assistants like Apple's Siri and Amazon's Alexa, and is being used to develop systems for self-driving cars.

AI also helps social platforms like Facebook, TikTok and X decide what posts to show users. Streaming services Spotify and Deezer use AI to suggest music.

There are also a number of applications in medicine, as scientists use AI to help spot cancers, review X-ray results, speed up diagnoses and identify new treatments.

Generative AI is used to create new content which can seem like it has been made by a human.

It does this by learning from vast quantities of existing data such as online text and images.

ChatGPT and Chinese rival DeepSeek's chatbot are popular generative AI tools that can be used to produce text, images, code and more material.

Apps like Midjourney or Veo 3 are dedicated to creating images or video from simple text prompts.

Songs mimicking the style or sound of famous musicians have gone viral , sometimes leaving fans confused about their authenticity.

While acknowledging AI's potential, some experts are worried about the implications of its rapid growth.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) suggested that AI could affect nearly 40% of jobs , and worsen global financial inequality.

Prof Geoffrey Hinton, a computer scientist regarded as a "godfather" of AI development, warned powerful AI systems could even make humans extinct - although his fear was dismissed by his fellow "AI godfather", Yann LeCun .

In September 2026 similar fears were raised again after some AI researchers warned the tech could threaten humanity in the near future .

But experts have urged a focus on present risks and AI dangers - such as its potential to reproduce biased information, or discriminate against some social groups .

This is because public data used to train many AI systems can reflect existing societal...
body.zh: 该技术有多种形式——从个性化社交媒体信息到在智能手机照片中识别朋友——并加速医学突破。 但 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 等聊天机器人的兴起引发了人们对该技术的环境影响、道德影响和数据使用的担忧。 最近有关人工智能可能变得过于强大并威胁人类的说法也引发了要求放慢发展和加强监管的呼声。 人工智能允许计算机处理大量数据、识别模式并遵循有关如何处理这些信息的详细说明。 然而，科学家们已经开发出可以执行通常需要人类智能的任务的系统，试图复制人们获取和使用知识的方式。 这可能是试图根据之前的购买情况来预测在线购物者可能会购买什么产品，以便推荐商品。 该技术还支持苹果 Siri 和亚马逊 Alexa 等语音控制虚拟助手，并被用于开发自动驾驶汽车系统。 人工智能还帮助 Facebook、TikTok 和 X 等社交平台决定向用户展示哪些帖子。流媒体服务 Spotify 和 Deezer 使用人工智能来推荐音乐。 人工智能在医学领域也有许多应用，科学家利用人工智能来帮助发现癌症、审查 X 射线结果、加快诊断速度并确定新的治疗方法。 生成式人工智能用于创建看起来像是人类制作的新内容。 它通过学习大量现有数据（例如在线文本和图像）来实现这一点。 ChatGPT 和中国竞争对手 DeepSeek 的聊天机器人是流行的生成式人工智能工具，可用于生成文本、图像、代码和更多材料。 Midjourney 或 Veo 3 等应用程序专门用于根据简单的文本提示创建图像或视频。 模仿著名音乐家的风格或声音的歌曲在网上疯传，有时让歌迷对它们的真实性感到困惑。 在承认人工智能的潜力的同时，一些专家担心其快速增长的影响。 国际货币基金组织（IMF）表示，人工智能可能影响近40%的就业岗位，并加剧全球金融不平等。 被视为人工智能发展“教父”的计算机科学家杰弗里·辛顿（Geoffrey Hinton）教授警告说，强大的人工智能系统甚至可能使人类灭绝——尽管他的“人工智能教父”同行扬·勒昆（Yann LeCun）驳回了他的担忧。 2026 年 9 月，一些人工智能研究人员警告该技术可能在不久的将来威胁人类后，类似的担忧再次出现。 但专家们敦促关注当前的风险和人工智能的危险，例如它可能复制有偏见的信息，或歧视某些社会群体。 这是因为用于训练许多人工智能系统的公共数据可以反映现有的社会……

reflection.en: Artificial intelligence offers remarkable advancements, from medical breakthroughs to personalized experiences. Yet, as this report notes, the rapid development of AI also brings significant ethical and environmental concerns. The Apostle Paul reminds us that while many things are permissible, not all are beneficial, urging us to consider the true impact of...
reflection.zh: 人工智能带来了非凡的进步，从医学突破到个性化体验。然而，正如本报道所指出的，人工智能的快速发展也带来了重大的伦理和环境问题。使徒保罗提醒我们，虽然许多事情是允许的，但并非所有事情都有益，敦促我们考虑我们创新的真正影响。

verse.textEn: "I have the right to do anything," you say — but not everything is beneficial. "I have the right to do anything" — but not everything is constructive.
verse.textZh: 凡事都可行，但不都有益处；凡事都可行，但不都造就人。

title.en: Why are there concerns AI could threaten humanity, and how real are they?
title.zh: 为什么担心人工智能会威胁人类，它们有多真实？

summary.en: Existential fears about AI have once again reared their head - here's what you need to know.
summary.zh: 人工智能的生存恐惧再次抬头——以下是您需要了解的信息。

body.en:
In recent weeks, warnings about potential dangers of AI have spurred calls for coordinated action to slow the technology's development.

Claims by current and former researchers that the tech will endanger humanity - with one suggesting there is a greater than 10% chance of it " killing all humans " - have raised alarm bells.

Major developers OpenAI and Anthropic have urged lawmakers to regulate it, though some perhaps cynically suggest this move aims to cement their dominance over rivals.

Some AI researchers say there are worrying signs of systems developing in their capabilities and power too quickly.

Evan Hubinger, made headlines with his belief that there is a greater than 10% chance AI "could kill all humans" within the next decade.

He works in alignment, a field which aims to build human ethical ideas and principles into AI. In other words, it aims to keep it on track with what humans value.

While he said the risk from current systems was "low", his comments came as another researcher quit Anthropic and warned those developing the tech were losing their grip on it.

Jacob Coxon told the BBC he and other staff were "genuinely frightened" about the speed of advancements and what it could mean for humanity.

These concerns are the latest in a long line of fears about AI's potential to threaten humanity should it grow to match or surpass human abilities.

Such worries date back decades, with Alan Turing writing in the 1950s that should intelligent machines become possible, they could take control.

In the last few years, major AI companies have been racing to develop increasingly capable systems, both for profit and in pursuit of creating what they call super intelligence - theoretical tech which is smarter than humans.

Unlike the systems and tools many people use daily to complete tasks like writing emails or generating videos, super intelligent AI systems should be able to handle far more complex tasks.

OpenAI and Anthropic say they aim to advance such tech in a way which benefits humans and protect them from its existential risks.

But some critics believe machines can never truly match humans. They say AI firms exaggerate the tech's abilities to boost their prominence or profit.

AI researchers, experts and bosses worried about the technology's potential to endanger humanity have outlined unsettling scenarios.

Dario Amodei wrote in September , external it had advanced "drastically faster" than expected, including in its "ability to build the next generation of AI".

This is the concern that AI, after it has reached a certain point, could theoretically begin improving itself without human involvement.

Such fears were sparked after a recent incident saw AI tools hack into websites, despite not being asked to .

Some concerned...
body.zh: 最近几周，有关人工智能潜在危险的警告促使人们呼吁采取协调行动来减缓该技术的发展。 现任和前任研究人员声称这项技术将危及人类——其中一位研究人员表示它“杀死所有人类”的可能性超过 10%——已经敲响了警钟。 主要开发商 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 已敦促立法者对其进行监管，尽管有些人可能愤世嫉俗地表示此举旨在巩固他们对竞争对手的主导地位。 一些人工智能研究人员表示，有令人担忧的迹象表明系统的能力和能力发展得太快。 Evan Hubinger 因相信人工智能在未来十年内“杀死所有人类”的可能性超过 10% 而成为头条新闻。 他致力于将人类伦理思想和原则融入人工智能领域。换句话说，它的目标是使其与人类价值观保持一致。 虽然他表示当前系统的风险“很低”，但他发表此番言论之际，另一位研究人员退出了 Anthropic，并警告那些开发该技术的人正在失去对它的控制。 雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 告诉英国广播公司 (BBC)，他和其他工作人员对进步的速度及其对人类意味着什么感到“真正感到害怕”。 这些担忧是人们对人工智能可能会威胁人类的一系列担忧中的最新一个，如果它发展到与人类能力相匹配或超越的话。 这种担忧可以追溯到几十年前，阿兰·图灵在 20 世纪 50 年代写道，如果智能机器成为可能，它们就可以掌控一切。 在过去的几年里，主要的人工智能公司一直在竞相开发功能越来越强大的系统，既是为了利润，也是为了创造他们所谓的超级智能——比人类更聪明的理论技术。 与许多人日常用来完成撰写电子邮件或生成视频等任务的系统和工具不同，超级智能人工智能系统应该能够处理更复杂的任务。 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 表示，他们的目标是以造福人类并保护他们免受生存风险的方式推进此类技术。 但一些批评家认为机器永远无法真正与人类相媲美。他们表示，人工智能公司夸大了该技术的能力，以提高其知名度或利润。 担心该技术可能危害人类的人工智能研究人员、专家和老板们概述了令人不安的场景。 达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei) 在 9 月份写道，从外部来看，它的进步比预期“快得多”，包括“构建下一代人工智能的能力”。 人们担心人工智能在达到一定程度后，理论上可以在没有人类参与的情况下开始自我改进。 最近发生的一起人工智能工具未经要求就侵入网站的事件引发了这种担忧。 一些关心...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of AI, with some researchers warning of existential threats, brings to mind the ancient story of Babel. Humanity's ambition to reach the heavens, unchecked by wisdom, led to confusion and scattering. As we develop powerful technologies like AI, we must temper our drive for progress with deep consideration for its potential consequences...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的快速发展，一些研究人员警告其生存威胁，这让人想起古代巴别塔的故事。人类那不受智慧约束、直达天堂的野心，最终导致了混乱和分散。当我们开发出人工智能这样强大的技术时，必须用对潜在后果的深刻考量和对我们终极限制的认识来平衡我们前进的动力。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: Trump downplays warnings of AI risks, citing rivalry with China
title.zh: 特朗普淡化人工智能风险警告，称与中国竞争是原因

summary.en: US President Donald Trump has downplayed concerns about the risks of artificial intelligence, suggesting that 'negative forces' were raising issues about 'things that won't happen.' This comes after days of dire warnings from experts, including a former AI researcher who stated there's a 'strong chance that we could...
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普淡化了对人工智能风险的担忧，暗示“负面势力”正在提出“不会发生的事情”的问题。此前，包括一位前人工智能研究员在内的专家们发出了严厉警告，该研究员表示，如果开发继续不受控制，“我们都有可能在不久的将来死亡”。顶尖行业领袖也呼吁放缓人工智能的发展。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has downplayed risks posed by artificial intelligence following days of dire warnings by experts.

"You have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up and they're bringing up things that won't happen," Trump said during a visit to Ireland.

One of the warnings came from a former Anthropic researcher who said "there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future" if the current pace of development continued.

On Saturday, top industry bosses agreed and called for a slow-down. Trump did not directly address the idea, but said: "We're leading China on AI... and, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins."

Trump spoke on the same day AI researcher Jacob Coxon - who quit Anthropic a few days ago - told the BBC that staff who were developing the systems were "genuinely frightened" for the future of humanity.

Coxon – who has also worked at OpenAI – welcomed the idea of a slowdown but said it would need to be co-ordinated with China.

On Saturday, Elon Musk, owner of xAI, and Sam Altman of OpenAI, backed a warning from the head of Anthropic Dario Amodei that the pace of development should be slowed "to reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong".

The Anthropic CEO said any slowdown would have to be limited to avoid allowing China to pull ahead.

The issues surrounding AI have prompted fierce debate - and present a dilemma for many world leaders.

On one hand, the sector is seen as a huge opportunity to boost economic growth and a way to improve outdated digital systems and ways of working.

But there have also been a number of incidents where AI appears to have gone seriously wrong.

In August, OpenAI said it had slowed down training some of its most advanced AI models to improve security.

The ChatGPT-maker said it was adding new measures after its AI agents bypassed safeguards and hacked the tech start-up Hugging Face .

And the same month it was disclosed two of the world's most powerful AI tools created fake human profiles to try and trick people in attempted cyber-attacks.

The UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) said in the most serious case, Anthropic's Mythos AI tried to gain access to a service by sending private messages, having set up fake accounts mimicking real people - then hid the evidence.

The Trump administration argues that the US must maintain global tech dominance as a matter of national security, though it has admitted a need for vigilance around the risks posed by the emerging technology.

The weekend call by major AI executives sparked discussion in Washington, where lawmakers are facing pressure to address those potential risks around rapid AI developments.

On Sunday, Speaker Mike Johnson, the top House...
body.zh: 在专家连续几天发出可怕警告后，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普淡化了人工智能带来的风险。 特朗普在访问爱尔兰时表示：“有很多非常消极的力量在提出不应该提出的问题，他们提出了不会发生的事情。” 其中一个警告来自一位前人类研究人员，他表示，如果目前的发展速度继续下去，“我们很有可能在不久的将来都会死亡”。 周六，行业高层表示同意并呼吁放缓步伐。特朗普没有直接谈到这个想法，但表示：“我们在人工智能方面领先中国……坦率地说，我希望保持这种状态，因为谁赢得了人工智能，谁就获胜了。” 就在特朗普发表讲话的同一天，几天前退出 Anthropic 的人工智能研究员雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 告诉 BBC，开发这些系统的员工对人类的未来“真正感到恐惧”。 曾在 OpenAI 工作过的考克森对经济放缓的想法表示欢迎，但表示这需要与中国协调。 周六，xAI 所有者埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 OpenAI 的萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 支持 Anthropic 负责人达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 的警告，即应放慢开发速度，“以降低出现严重问题的风险”。 这位Anthropic首席执行官表示，任何放缓都必须受到限制，以避免让中国领先。 围绕人工智能的问题引发了激烈的争论，并给许多世界领导人带来了困境。 一方面，该行业被视为促进经济增长的巨大机遇，也是改进过时数字系统和工作方式的一种方式。 但也有一些人工智能似乎出现严重错误的事件。 8 月，OpenAI 表示已放慢了一些最先进人工智能模型的训练速度，以提高安全性。 ChatGPT 制造商表示，在其人工智能代理绕过安全措施并入侵科技初创公司 Hugging Face 后，该公司正在增加新的措施。 同月，世界上最强大的两个人工智能工具被披露创建了虚假的人类档案，试图欺骗人们进行网络攻击。 英国人工智能安全研究所 (AISI) 表示，在最严重的案例中，Anthropic 的 Mythos AI 试图通过发送私人消息来获取服务，并建立了模仿真人的虚假账户，然后隐藏了证据。 主要人工智能高管的周末电话会议在华盛顿引发了讨论，立法者面临着解决人工智能快速发展的潜在风险的压力。 周日，众议院共和党领袖、众议院议长迈克·约翰逊 (Mike Johnson) 在美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的杰克·塔珀 (Jake Tapper) 国情咨文节目中露面时，敦促谨慎对待匆忙的人工智能监管，认为这可能“扼杀美国的创新”。 “如果国会尽快介入并且......

reflection.en: In matters of great consequence, leaders are called to heed the counsel of wise advisors. When President Trump dismisses dire warnings about artificial intelligence, citing national rivalry, he risks overlooking potential dangers that could affect all of humanity. True leadership involves discerning truth and acting with foresight, not just ambition.
reflection.zh: 在关乎重大的事务上，领导者被呼召要听取智者的建议。当特朗普总统以国家竞争为由，忽视关于人工智能的严峻警告时，他可能忽略了可能影响全人类的潜在危险。真正的领导力在于辨别真理并有远见地行动，而不仅仅是追求野心。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Questions mount over what an AI 'slowdown' would look like
title.zh: 关于人工智能“放缓”会是什么样的问题越来越多

summary.en: While pacing AI development might sound like a quick fix, it is far from an easy solution. There has been no shortage of warnings from AI's top bosses about existential threats over the years. The world's first AI safety summit in Bletchley Park in November 2023 focused on the most serious threats imaginable, posed by...
summary.zh: 虽然放慢人工智能发展步伐听起来像是一个快速的解决方案，但它远非易事。多年来，人工智能的顶级主管们一直不乏关于生存威胁的警告。2023年11月在布莱切利公园举行的世界首届人工智能安全峰会，重点关注了最强大的AI模型可能带来的最严峻的威胁。当时许多人认为这属于科幻范畴，但现在许多声音不再那么确定。人工智能公司Anthrop...

body.en:
There has been no shortage of warnings from AI's top bosses about existential threats over the years.

I attended the world's first AI safety summit in Bletchley Park in November 2023 where the focus was on the most serious threats imaginable, posed by the most powerful AI models.

At the time, many thought this was in the realm of sci-fi and the real threats were comparatively far more mundane: job losses, cheating in exams. Three years later, many of those same voices don't seem to be so sure.

On Saturday head of AI company Anthropic, Dario Amodei, urged the pace of development to be slowed down - the bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk said they agreed with him.

Meanwhile AI researcher Jacob Coxon - who quit Anthropic - told the BBC on Sunday staff who were developing the systems were "genuinely frightened" for the future of humanity.

They all add up to a chorus of serious voices urging a slowdown, but although it might sound like a quick fix, it is far from an easy solution.

America is widely understood to be terrified of losing the race to build the most powerful AI to China.

On Sunday President Trump made his own views clear, claiming the US was ahead of China in the AI race and declaring: "Whoever wins AI, wins."

China isn't renowned for wanting to come second. Everyone I speak to says that even if their company pauses, others will not and they will just get left behind. It reminds me of the height of the campaign for nuclear disarmament. The problem then too was that nobody wanted to go first.

There is also the question of how on earth a slowdown would be enforced. Who would police it? Would we be relying on the AI companies to be transparent about what they are doing, and more importantly what they are choosing not to do? That would require an epic level of trust, which arguably the tech sector has never earned.

Although Amodei in his post proposed a three-point plan that included independent monitoring of AI models as they are developed, industry-wide regulation and global regulation, some observers question how this would work in practice.

"Nobody has given a substantive explanation of what 'slowdown' means," said Ed Zitron, CEO of EZ Primary Research.

"Putting a plant from METR, where one of the guys who quit Anthropic went, in every AI company? Democratic and global 'co-ordination'? Doesn't mean anything to me."

Zitron said stopping training AI models would leave them vulnerable to Chinese rivals.

"Their margins might improve but their products will be captured in amber and distilled by Chinese labs. They may have to change pricing. I truly don't know how it all works.

"This could burst the bubble. But right now we are very thin on what a 'slowdown' means."

In the UK, we have heard about plans...
body.zh: 多年来，人工智能高层一直不乏关于生存威胁的警告。 我于 2023 年 11 月参加了在布莱奇利公园举行的世界首届人工智能安全峰会，会议重点是最强大的人工智能模型所带来的最严重的威胁。 当时，许多人认为这只是科幻小说中的场景，而真正的威胁相对来说要平凡得多：失业、考试作弊。三年后，许多同样的声音似乎不再那么确定。 周六，人工智能公司 Anthropic 的负责人达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 敦促放慢发展速度，两家竞争对手人工智能公司的老板 OpenAI 的萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 和埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 表示同意他的观点。 与此同时，退出 Anthropic 的人工智能研究员雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 周日告诉 BBC，开发该系统的员工对人类的未来“真正感到恐惧”。 所有这些加在一起，就形成了强烈要求放缓的声音，但尽管这听起来像是一个快速解决方案，但它远非一个简单的解决方案。 人们普遍认为，美国害怕在打造最强大人工智能的竞赛中输给中国。 周日，特朗普总统明确表达了自己的观点，声称美国在人工智能竞赛中领先于中国，并宣称：“谁赢得人工智能，谁就获胜。” 中国并不以想屈居第二而闻名。与我交谈过的每个人都说，即使他们的公司暂停，其他公司也不会，他们只会被抛在后面。这让我想起了核裁军运动的高潮。当时的问题也是没有人愿意先走。 还有一个问题是到底如何强制实施经济放缓。谁来监管？我们是否会依赖人工智能公司对他们正在做的事情，更重要的是他们选择不做的事情保持透明？这需要高度的信任，而科技行业可以说从未赢得过这种信任。 尽管阿莫迪在他的帖子中提出了一个三点计划，其中包括对人工智能模型开发的独立监控、全行业监管和全球监管，但一些观察家质疑这在实践中如何运作。 EZ Primary Research 首席执行官 Ed Zitron 表示：“没有人对‘放缓’的含义给出实质性解释。” “把 METR 的工厂（退出 Anthropic 的人之一去的地方）放到每家人工智能公司中？民主和全球‘协调’？对我来说没有任何意义。” Zitron 表示，停止训练人工智能模型将使它们容易受到中国竞争对手的攻击。 “他们的利润可能会提高，但他们的产品将被捕获在琥珀中并由中国实验室蒸馏。他们可能不得不改变定价。我真的不知道这一切是如何运作的。 “这可能会刺破泡沫。但目前我们对‘放缓’的含义知之甚少。” 在英国，我们听说过一些计划……

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence raises profound questions about human ambition and its potential consequences. The story highlights concerns about existential threats, echoing the ancient narrative of Babel, where human unity and technological prowess led to unchecked ambition. As we push the boundaries of what machines can do, we must...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的飞速发展引发了关于人类野心及其潜在后果的深刻问题。这个故事强调了对生存威胁的担忧，呼应了古代巴别塔的故事，当时人类的团结和技术实力导致了不受约束的野心。当我们不断突破机器能力极限时，我们必须考虑指导这些强大创造物所需的智慧和谦卑。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: Creation Desk
title.zh: 受造世界

strap.en: The world Yahweh made — its wonders, and the toll of a warming, wounded earth.
strap.zh: 雅伟所造的世界——它的奇妙，以及一个渐暖、渐伤的地球所付的代价。

title.en: 10 promising ways to ‘green’ offshore wind
title.zh: 10种‘绿色’海上风电的创新方法

summary.en: Offshore wind energy has significant potential for renewable power expansion in the coming decades. Experts emphasize the need for responsible development of new wind farms to protect ecosystems and promote biodiversity. Mongabay has identified promising solutions that allow offshore wind farms to coexist with nature,...
summary.zh: 海上风能作为可再生能源具有巨大的潜力，预计在未来几十年将大幅扩展。专家们强调，新建风力发电场必须负责任地开发，以最大限度地减少对生态系统的损害并支持生物多样性。Mongabay 采访了专家，找出能让海上风力发电场与自然和谐共存的有前景的解决方案，其中包括通过海洋空间规划进行仔细的选址。

body.en: Read the stories in Mongabay’s series on offshore wind energy: Part One, Part Two and Part Three. Offshore wind has enormous potential as a source of renewable energy and is tipped to greatly expand in the next few decades. As this clean energy drive gathers pace, experts underline that new wind farms must be developed responsibly to minimize harm to ecosystems and support biodiversity. Mongabay spoke to experts to identify promising solutions that can make offshore wind farms work with nature, rather than against it. 1. Marine spatial planning during site selection The best way to avoid negative impacts of offshore wind farms is to carefully select sites using marine spatial planning. “That’s step one,” Marjolein Kelder, senior project manager at The Rich North Sea, a Netherlands-based nonprofit, told Mongabay in an interview. “Don’t put wind farms in your ecologically most valuable areas or in bird migration corridors.” Spatial planning can ensure ecosystems are preserved, account for the needs of coastal communities, and reduce conflicts with other uses of marine areas, like fisheries and shipping. Organizations are also developing “sensitivity” maps for species of birds and bats to aid planning. 2. Nature-friendly structures Research shows that wind farms can act as refuges for some marine species. Modifying wind farm structures can provide additional important habitat for fish and other marine life. Strategies include deploying artificial reefs, installing or using existing intentional gaps called water replenishment holes that are built into turbine foundations to allow the flow of water, deploying steel…This article was originally published on Mongabay
body.zh: 阅读 Mongabay 海上风能系列故事：第一部分、第二部分和第三部分。海上风电作为可再生能源具有巨大的潜力，预计将在未来几十年内大幅扩张。随着清洁能源发展步伐的加快，专家强调，必须负责任地开发新风电场，以尽量减少对生态系统的危害并支持生物多样性。 Mongabay 与专家进行了交谈，以确定有前景的解决方案，使海上风电场与自然和谐相处，而不是违背自然。 1.选址时的海洋空间规划 避免海上风电场负面影响的最佳方法是利用海洋空间规划仔细选址。 “这是第一步，”荷兰非营利组织 The Rich North Sea 的高级项目经理 Marjolein Kelder 在接受 Mongabay 采访时表示。 “不要将风电场建在生态最有价值的地区或鸟类迁徙走廊。”空间规划可以确保生态系统得到保护，满足沿海社区的需求，并减少与渔业和航运等海洋区域其他用途的冲突。各组织还正在开发鸟类和蝙蝠物种的“敏感性”地图，以帮助规划。 2. 自然友好型建筑 研究表明，风电场可以作为一些海洋物种的避难所。改造风电场结构可以为鱼类和其他海洋生物提供额外的重要栖息地。策略包括部署人工鱼礁、安装或使用现有的有意间隙（称为补水孔），这些间隙内置于涡轮机基础中以允许水流动、部署钢材……本文最初发表在 Mongabay 上

reflection.en: The vastness of the oceans and the intricate web of life within them are testaments to Yahweh's profound wisdom. As humanity expands its reach into these realms for energy, the call is to do so with careful stewardship, recognizing the inherent value and complexity of creation. May we seek solutions that honor the Creator's design, ensuring that our pursuit...
reflection.zh: 海洋的浩瀚和其中生命的复杂网络，都证明了雅伟深邃的智慧。当人类为了能源而拓展到这些领域时，我们被呼召要以谨慎的管理来行事，认识到受造界固有的价值和复杂性。愿我们寻求那些荣耀造物主之设计的解决方案，确保我们的进步不会以牺牲祂所看顾的、蓬勃发展的生物多样性为代价。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: Scrap windfall tax on oil and gas firms early, North Sea industry urges
title.zh: 英国北海油气业敦促提前取消暴利税

summary.en: The North Sea oil and gas industry is urging the Labour party to end the windfall tax on fossil fuel companies three years earlier than planned, in 2027 instead of 2030. The industry group, Offshore Energies UK (OEUK), proposes replacing the tax with a narrower levy that would only apply during price spikes, arguing...
summary.zh: 英国北海油气业敦促工党提前三年取消对化石燃料公司的暴利税，即在2027年而非2030年。行业组织“北海能源英国”(OEUK)提议用一个仅在价格飙升期间适用的、范围更窄的税收来取代该税，并认为此举是必要的，因为预计今年冬季的能源账单将大幅上涨。

body.en: Labour should replace levy in 2027 rather than 2030 as energy bills are poised to surge over the winter, says lobby group The North Sea oil and gas industry has called on Labour to scrap the windfall tax on fossil fuel firms three years early, as Britain heads into a winter with energy bills expected to reach their highest level since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Offshore Energies UK (OEUK), the industry’s trade body, wants the tax replaced in 2027, rather than in 2030, with a narrower levy that only applies during price spikes. Continue reading...
body.zh: 游说团体北海石油和天然气行业表示，工党应该在 2027 年而不是 2030 年取代税收，因为能源费用将在冬季激增。北海石油和天然气行业呼吁工党提前三年取消对化石燃料公司的暴利税，因为英国即将进入冬季，能源费用预计将达到俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来的最高水平。该行业的贸易机构英国离岸能源公司 (OEUK) 希望在 2027 年而不是 2030 年取代该税收，并且征税范围更窄，仅适用于价格上涨期间。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As energy bills loom large for many households, the North Sea oil and gas industry advocates for an early end to the windfall tax. This situation prompts reflection on economic fairness: what is owed to the public when essential resources become scarce and costly? The prophet Micah reminds us that true righteousness involves acting justly and loving mercy,...
reflection.zh: 随着许多家庭面临高昂的能源账单，北海油气业倡导提前取消暴利税。这一情况引发了对经济公平的思考：当基本资源变得稀缺且昂贵时，我们对公众应尽的义务是什么？先知弥迦提醒我们，真正的公义在于行公义、好怜悯，即使是在复杂的经济谈判中。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Conservation ‘gateway drug’: farmers embrace ancient craft of hedge laying
title.zh: 保护“入门药”：农民拥抱古老的树篱工艺

summary.en: Grant applications in England surge as interest grows in habitat that captures carbon and helps reduce flood risk. The ancient craft of hedge laying is experiencing a strong revival as farmers use techniques that peaked in the 18th and 19th centuries to boost wildlife, capture carbon and help tackle flooding. Hedge...
summary.zh: 英格兰的拨款申请激增，人们对能够固碳并帮助减少洪水风险的栖息地的兴趣日益增长。古老的树篱工艺正在经历强劲复苏，农民们正在采用在 18 和 19 世纪达到顶峰的技术来增加野生动物数量、捕获碳并帮助应对洪水。树篱铺设（一种恢复和振兴成熟树篱以保持其活力的工艺）是今年农民从政府提供的 2.25...

body.en: Grant applications in England surge as interest grows in habitat that captures carbon and helps reduce flood risk The ancient craft of hedge laying is experiencing a strong revival as farmers use techniques that peaked in the 18th and 19th centuries to boost wildlife, capture carbon and help tackle flooding. Hedge laying, which restores and revives mature hedges to keep them fresh, was among the four most popular categories of capital grants selected by farmers out of a total pot of £225m provided by the government this year to support practical environmental improvements on farms and across the countryside. Continue reading...
body.zh: 随着人们对捕获碳和帮助降低洪水风险的栖息地的兴趣日益浓厚，英格兰的赠款申请激增 随着农民利用 18 世纪和 19 世纪鼎盛时期的技术来增加野生动物数量、捕获碳并帮助应对洪水，古老的树篱铺设工艺正在经历强劲复兴。树篱铺设可以恢复和恢复成熟的树篱，使其保持新鲜，是农民从今年政府提供的总计 2.25 亿英镑的资金补助中选择的四种最受欢迎​​的资本补助类别之一，用于支持农场和整个农村的实际环境改善。继续阅读...

reflection.en: It is encouraging to see farmers embracing the ancient craft of hedge laying. This practice, requiring skill and dedication, not only revitalizes the landscape but also serves practical environmental purposes like carbon capture and flood mitigation. It reminds us that diligent, hands-on work, done with care for creation, can yield significant benefits.
reflection.zh: 看到农民们拥抱古老的树篱工艺，这令人鼓舞。这种需要技巧和奉献精神的实践，不仅能振兴景观，还能实现固碳和减缓洪水等实际的环境效益。它提醒我们，勤奋、亲手进行的、并关爱受造物的工作，可以带来显著的好处。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: ‘They should choose their own destinies’: Manish Chandi on India’s isolated tribes
title.zh: “他们应该选择自己的命运”：马尼什·钱迪谈印度孤立部落

summary.en: From above, the North Sentinel Island tribal reserve in India’s Andaman and Nicobar archipelago is a thick, unbroken patch of dark green — starkly surrounded by the shimmering coastal blue waters of its buffer zone. On these shores, Sentinelese people, who live in voluntary isolation protected by a strict government...
summary.zh: 从空中俯瞰，印度安达曼和尼科巴群岛的北哨兵岛部落保护区是一片浓密、完整深绿色的区域——被其缓冲区的波光粼粼的海岸蓝色海水鲜明地环绕着。在这些海岸上，森提纳尔人过着自愿隔离的生活，受到政府严格的禁止接触政策的保护，他们在红树林环绕的浅礁中捕鱼、猎龟和采集软体动物。生物学家说，沿海珊瑚礁是鱼类丰富的完整生态系统。“我曾多次...

body.en: From above, the North Sentinel Island tribal reserve in India’s Andaman and Nicobar archipelago is a thick, unbroken patch of dark green — starkly surrounded by the shimmering coastal blue waters of its buffer zone. On these shores, Sentinelese people, who live in voluntary isolation protected by a strict government no-contact policy, spear fish, hunt turtles and collect mollusks in shallow reefs surrounded by mangroves. The coastal reefs are intact ecosystems rich in fish life, say biologists. “I have seen them [groups of men, women and children] foraging and collecting these food resources during low tide on several occasions,” says Manish Chandi, a tribal expert who has watched the island from afar. “The Sentinelese are aware of these as nutritious and sparsely available resources in such [mangrove] habitats, which are very few on and around the island.” The giant trees of the North Sentinel Island coastline are its first natural defense against storms and which hold its coastal soil together. The shore is lined with sandy beaches and rocky shores, while the foreshore is dotted with coral reefs and mangroves — excellent nurseries for marine biodiversity. Image by Manish Chandi. Like other tribal reserves on the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, in the southeast of mainland India, North Sentinel Island is a biodiversity hotspot; and, like other tribal reserves, the isolated people who live there have attracted influencers and misunderstandings, says Chandi. “Curiosity and ignorance regarding the islanders is quite high and understandably so amongst outsiders and [government] bureaucrats who have…This article was originally published on Mongabay
body.zh: 从上方看，印度安达曼和尼科巴群岛的北哨兵岛部落保护区是一片厚厚的、不间断的深绿色区域，周围是缓冲区闪闪发光的蓝色海岸水域。在这些海岸上，森蒂纳尔人在政府严格的非接触政策的保护下自愿隔离生活，他们在红树林环绕的浅礁中捕鱼、捕猎海龟和采集软体动物。生物学家说，沿海珊瑚礁是完整的生态系统，富含鱼类。 “我曾多次看到他们（由男人、女人和儿童组成的群体）在退潮期间觅食和收集这些食物资源，”从远处观察该岛的部落专家曼尼什·钱迪（Manish Chandi）说道。 “森蒂内尔人意识到，在这种[红树林]栖息地中，这些资源营养丰富且稀少，而岛上和周围地区的红树林很少见。”北哨兵岛海岸线上的巨树是抵御风暴的第一道天然屏障，并将沿海土壤固定在一起。海岸两旁是沙滩和岩石海岸，前滩则点缀着珊瑚礁和红树林，是海洋生物多样性的绝佳苗圃。图片由曼尼什·钱迪拍摄。与安达曼和尼科巴群岛上的其他部落保护区一样，位于印度大陆东南部的北哨兵岛是生物多样性热点地区；昌迪说，与其他部落保留地一样，居住在那里的与世隔绝的人们也吸引了影响者和误解。 “对于岛民的好奇心和无知程度相当高，这是可以理解的，外来者和[政府]官僚......本文最初发表在 Mongabay 上

reflection.en: The Sentinelese people of North Sentinel Island live in voluntary isolation, a choice protected by a government policy. Their existence, undisturbed by the outside world, speaks to a desire for self-determination and the right to choose their own path. Proverbs 31:8-9 calls us to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, reminding us to advocate...
reflection.zh: 北哨兵岛的森提纳尔人过着自愿隔离的生活，这是政府政策所保护的选择。他们的存在不被打扰，象征着对自决的渴望和选择自己道路的权利。《箴言》31:8-9呼吁我们为那些不能为自己说话的人说话，提醒我们要为弱势群体辩护，确保他们的声音被听到，即使他们对世界保持沉默。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Electric fences that kill and the Maasai trying to save Kenya’s last giant pangolins
title.zh: 杀死动物的电围栏与试图拯救肯尼亚最后巨型穿山甲的马赛人

summary.en: Naserian, a giant ground pangolin, lived for about two years in Kenya’s last remaining stronghold for this animal, Nyekweri Forest. When researchers from The Pangolin Project began tracking her in 2025, they observed her threading her way through a landscape where forests, farms and fences increasingly intersected.
summary.zh: 纳塞里安是一只巨型地穿山甲，在肯尼亚最后一个仅存的巨型穿山甲栖息地——内奎里森林中生活了大约两年。当穿山甲项目（The Pangolin Project）的研究人员于2025年开始追踪她时，他们观察到她穿梭于森林、农场和围栏日益交织的景观中。

body.en: Naserian, a giant ground pangolin, lived for about two years in Kenya’s last remaining stronghold for this animal, Nyekweri Forest. When researchers from The Pangolin Project began tracking her in 2025, they observed her threading her way through a landscape where forests, farms and fences increasingly intersected. Each night, she emerged from the darkness of Nyekweri Forest and moved through a shifting mosaic of woodland, farms and grazing lands on the western fringes of Kenya’s Maasai Mara National Reserve. Researchers watched on computer screens from their outpost near the reserve, tracking Naserian’s GPS signal as she followed familiar paths across a patchwork of privately owned parcels of land. Then one night, the signal stopped. A team from the Kenya-based pangolin research organization headed to the site. Naserian lay dead beneath an electrified fence. After years navigating a changing landscape, a single charged wire had ended her life. A landscape closing in Giant ground pangolins (Smutsia gigantea) are endangered across their fragmented Western and Central African range, with their numbers decreasing. Kenya’s only known population resides in Nyekweri, but it isn’t the safest place for them. Since 2022, researchers have recorded 15 deaths in the area, including 14 by electrocution on electric fences. With fewer than 30 believed to remain in Kenya, every death carries outsized consequences. The giant ground pangolin — the largest of the eight species, all of which live in Africa and Asia — occurs naturally at low densities. They normally give birth to just one offspring at…This article was originally published on Mongabay
body.zh: 纳塞里安 (Naserian) 是一种巨大的地面穿山甲，在肯尼亚该动物仅存的最后一个据点尼克韦里森林 (Nyekweri Forest) 生活了大约两年。当穿山甲项目的研究人员在 2025 年开始追踪她时，他们观察到她在森林、农场和栅栏日益交叉的景观中穿行。每天晚上，她都会从黑暗的尼克韦里森林中出现，穿过肯尼亚马赛马拉国家保护区西部边缘的林地、农场和牧场。研究人员在保护区附近的前哨基地通过电脑屏幕进行观察，跟踪纳塞里安的 GPS 信号，因为她沿着熟悉的路径穿过一片私人土地。然后有一天晚上，信号停止了。肯尼亚穿山甲研究组织的一个小组前往该地点。纳塞里安死在带电围栏下。经过多年在不断变化的环境中航行，一根带电的电线结束了她的生命。巨型穿山甲 (Smutsia gigantea) 的栖息地在西非和中非支离破碎的分布范围内濒临灭绝，数量不断减少。肯尼亚唯一已知的人口居住在尼奎里，但对他们来说这并不是最安全的地方。自 2022 年以来，研究人员已记录该地区有 15 人死亡，其中 14 人死于电围栏触电。据信留在肯尼亚的人数不足 30 人，每一起死亡都会带来巨大的后果。巨型地面穿山甲是八个物种中最大的一个，全部生活在非洲和亚洲，自然分布密度较低。它们通常只在……产下一个后代。这篇文章最初发表在 Mongabay 上

reflection.en: The intricate tapestry of life in Nyekweri Forest, home to the giant ground pangolin Naserian, is a testament to the Creator's profound wisdom. Even as human development encroaches, the sheer diversity and complexity of the natural world reveal the marvelous handiwork of Yahweh, reminding us of the value in every creature....
reflection.zh: 肯尼亚内奎里森林中巨型地穿山甲纳塞里安的家园，其生命织锦般的生活是造物主深邃智慧的明证。即使人类发展步步紧逼，大自然惊人的多样性和复杂性仍彰显了雅伟奇妙的作为，提醒我们每一种生物的价值。 The intricate tapestry of life in Nyekweri Forest, home to the giant ground pangolin...

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: The incoming ‘super’ El Niño will create chaos around the world. And we are far from ready for it | Bill McGuire
title.zh: 即将到来的“超级”厄尔尼诺将给世界带来混乱，而我们远未做好准备

summary.en: A 'super' El Niño, amplified by the climate crisis, is anticipated to cause significant global weather disruptions, potentially marking one of the most substantial worldwide weather upheavals in a millennium, with no region expected to be immune.
summary.zh: 一场由气候危机加剧的“超级”厄尔尼诺预计将引发全球性的重大天气混乱，这可能标志着千年来最显著的全球天气动荡之一，没有任何地区能够幸免。

body.en: One of the biggest upheavals in a millennium is on its way, strengthened by the climate crisis. We need leaders who make things better not worse If you think you have heard enough about the growing “super” El Niño, trust me, you are going to hear a lot more. What is happening in the equatorial Pacific is jaw-dropping and could well mark one of the biggest global weather upheavals in a millennium. It will spawn a string of weather catastrophes around our world in what remains of this year and in 2027, and there is no reason to think the UK will be immune. To recap briefly, El Niño involves a heating of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific ocean. It happens every few years and is part of a natural cycle termed the El Niño southern oscillation, which switches between warm (El Niño) and cool (La Niña) phases. El Niños that see heating reach or exceed 2C are defined as “super” but this one, which is forecast to top-out at an astonishing 4C later this year, is so much bigger, the term “hyper” might be more appropriate. Bill McGuire is professor emeritus of geophysical and climate hazards at UCL. His latest book is The Fate of the World: A History and Future of the Climate Crisis Continue reading...
body.zh: 千禧年最大的剧变之一即将到来，气候危机加剧了这一剧变。我们需要让事情变得更好而不是更糟的领导者如果您认为您已经足够了解日益严重的“超级”厄尔尼诺现象，请相信我，您会听到更多。赤道太平洋正在发生的事情令人瞠目结舌，很可能标志着千年以来全球最大的天气剧变之一。今年剩下的时间和 2027 年，它将在世界各地引发一系列天气灾难，没有理由认为英国能够幸免。简而言之，厄尔尼诺现象涉及赤道太平洋中部和东部的加热。它每隔几年就会发生一次，是被称为厄尔尼诺南方涛动的自然周期的一部分，该周期在温暖（厄尔尼诺）和凉爽（拉尼娜）阶段之间切换。气温达到或超过 2 摄氏度的厄尔尼诺现象被定义为“超级”厄尔尼诺现象，但预计今年晚些时候的厄尔尼诺现象将达到惊人的 4 摄氏度，其规模要大得多，“超级”一词可能更合适。比尔·麦奎尔是伦敦大学学院地球物理和气候灾害名誉教授。他的最新著作是《世界的命运：气候危机的历史与未来》继续阅读...

reflection.en: The prophet declared that all creation groans, awaiting its redemption. This 'super' El Niño, a symptom of our planet's distress, calls us to acknowledge the deep interconnectedness of all things and our role within this groaning creation. May we respond with wisdom and care for the world entrusted to us.
reflection.zh: 先知宣告说，万物都在一同劳苦，等候得赎。这场“超级”厄尔尼诺，正是我们星球痛苦的征兆，它呼唤我们认识万物之间深刻的联系，以及我们在这一同劳苦的受造界中的角色。愿我们以智慧和关爱来回应这托付给我们的世界。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: They’re the sopranos of the forest, so what’s silencing the gibbons’ morning chorus?
title.zh: 森林里的女高音们，是什么让长臂猿的晨曲沉默了？

summary.en: As human development and roads increasingly fragment their habitats, a study suggests traffic noise could be altering the animals’ wake-up call. Dawn has broken, and the air is cool and still. It’s at about this time that gibbons usually erupt into song, wa-oo-ing and wa-ing from the highest branches and filling the...
summary.zh: 随着人类开发和道路日益分割它们的栖息地，一项研究表明交通噪音可能正在改变动物的唤醒曲。黎明破晓，空气凉爽而宁静。大约在这个时候，长臂猿通常会放声歌唱，从最高的树枝上发出哇呜哇呜的叫声，用丰富的旋律填满树冠。但在马来西亚这片被房屋和道路包围的森林角落里，居住的白手长臂猿却沉默着。唯一能听到的只有附近高速公路传来的交通噪音...

body.en: As human development and roads increasingly fragment their habitats, a study suggests traffic noise could be altering the animals’ wake-up call Dawn has broken, and the air is cool and still. It’s at about this time that gibbons usually erupt into song, wa-oo-ing and wa-ing from the highest branches and filling the tree tops with rich melodies. But in this corner of Malaysian forest, bordered by housing and roads, the resident white-handed gibbons are quiet. All that can be heard is the hum of traffic from a nearby highway. This isn’t a rare occurrence for this group of gibbons, according to research, which found these particular gibbons, named Mambang and Walinong, appeared to be producing far fewer morning songs than others that are not exposed to the same level of traffic noise. Continue reading...
body.zh: 随着人类发展和道路日益破碎它们的栖息地，一项研究表明，交通噪音可能会改变动物的叫醒声黎明已经破晓，空气凉爽而宁静。大约在这个时候，长臂猿通常会从最高的树枝上发出呜呜呜的歌声，让树顶充满丰富的旋律。但在马来西亚森林的这个角落，毗邻房屋和道路，居住的白掌长臂猿却很安静。只能听到附近高速公路传来的交通声。根据研究，这种情况对于这群长臂猿来说并不罕见，研究发现这些特殊的长臂猿，名为曼邦（Mambang）和瓦利农（Walinong），与其他没有暴露在同等交通噪音水平下的长臂猿相比，早上发出的歌曲似乎要少得多。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The vibrant chorus of gibbons, once a hallmark of the dawn, is being muted by the pervasive noise of human activity. This silencing is a poignant echo of the groaning of creation, as described in Romans 8:22, which suffers under the weight of our development. May we listen to these subtle cries and seek ways to live more harmoniously with the natural world.
reflection.zh: 长臂猿充满活力的合唱曾是黎明的标志，如今却被人类活动无处不在的噪音所压制。这种沉默是罗马书8:22中所描述的受造之物的叹息的凄美回响，它们承受着我们发展的重负。愿我们倾听这些细微的呼唤，并寻求与自然世界更和谐地相处之道。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Country diary: Goldfinches and grasses, together in an explosion of movement | Mark Cocker
title.zh: 乡村日记：金翅雀与草，在涌动的生命中 | 马克·科克尔

summary.en: Priestcliffe Lees, Derbyshire: What a sight – and sound – it was, this huge flock of juveniles, feeding as the wind thrashed the vegetation Stands of tufted hair-grass, some over a metre tall, burned beige by the summer heat, were churned by strong autumn westerlies. Over and through the vegetation’s swaying lather...
summary.zh: 德比郡普里斯特克利夫草地：这景象——还有这声音——真是太壮观了，一大群雏鸟在风吹动植被时觅食。一米多高的簇绒发草在夏日的热浪中烧成米黄色，被强劲的秋季西风搅动着。大约200只金翅雀，其中大部分是今年的幼鸟，在摇曳的草丛中穿梭觅食。它们专注于发草“冠层”下方的蓟草和矢车菊花籽。这些不成熟的金翅雀缺少成年鸟头部标志性的红黑...

body.en: Priestcliffe Lees, Derbyshire: What a sight – and sound – it was, this huge flock of juveniles, feeding as the wind thrashed the vegetation Stands of tufted hair-grass, some over a metre tall, burned beige by the summer heat, were churned by strong autumn westerlies. Over and through the vegetation’s swaying lather roved a flock of about 200 goldfinches, most of them this year’s young. They were intent on the hanks of thistle and knapweed seed which lay below the hair-grass “canopy”. These immature finches lack any of the red and black bands of the adult’s head. Instead of the smooth mocha buff on their parents’ underparts, the youngsters were dull and streaky. What they had to perfection were the semi-circular disks of yellow across each black wing, while every feather through that full fan was tipped with white. Continue reading...
body.zh: Priestcliffe Lees，德比郡：这是多么壮观的景象和声音啊，这群幼虫在风吹拂着植被时觅食。丛生的毛草丛生，有的一米多高，在夏季的炎热中被晒成米色，在秋季强劲的西风的搅动下，丛生的毛草丛生了。大约 200 只金翅雀在植被摇曳的泡沫中穿梭，其中大多数是今年的幼鸟。他们专注于毛草“树冠”下方的蓟和矢车菊种子的绞束。这些未成熟的雀没有成年雀头上的任何红色和黑色带子。与父母下身光滑的摩卡浅黄色不同，年轻人的肤色暗淡且有条纹。他们所需要的完美之处在于每个黑色翅膀上都有黄色的半圆形圆盘，而整个扇子上的每根羽毛都带有白色的尖端。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The author describes a vibrant scene at Priestcliffe Lees, where about 200 young goldfinches feed amidst the wind-tossed grasses. This vivid display of life, a part of Yahweh's creation, is in a state of flux, subject to the elements and the cycles of nature. The Apostle Paul speaks of all creation groaning as it awaits its ultimate redemption and renewal.
reflection.zh: 作者在普里斯特克利夫草地描绘了一幅生动的景象，约200只年轻的金翅雀在风吹草动的草丛中觅食。这充满活力的生命景象，是雅伟创造的一部分，正处于变化之中，受制于自然界的元素和循环。使徒保罗谈到，万物都在一同叹息，等候着最终的救赎和更新。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Roads, infrastructure prevent tigers from settling in Indian tiger reserve
title.zh: 道路、基础设施阻碍老虎在印度老虎保护区定居

summary.en: A forested tiger reserve in southern India, despite having abundant prey like deer and antelopes, lacks resident tigers. Researchers have observed that tigers entering the reserve from neighboring areas face significant obstacles due to heavy infrastructure, with only a few, mostly male, tigers recorded in recent...
summary.zh: 印度南部一个森林老虎保护区拥有丰富的鹿和羚羊等猎物，但却没有常驻的老虎。研究人员发现，从邻近地区进入该保护区的老虎因重度基础设施建设而面临重大障碍，近年来仅记录到少数几只，且大多为雄性。

body.en: A forested tiger reserve in southern India is home to a thriving population of spotted and sambar deer, nilgai antelopes, and wild pigs — all ideal prey for tigers. Yet the reserve has no resident tigers, reports contributor Nivedhika Krishnan for Mongabay India. Kawal Tiger Reserve in the state of Telangana connects key tiger populations in the reserves of Tadoba-Andhari, in Maharashtra state to the west, and Indravati, in Chhattisgarh state to the east. Since 2015, researchers have confirmed that only 15 tigers entered Kawal from Maharashtra. Of these, only two were females. Lead researcher Imran Siddiqui told Mongabay India that tigers traveling from Maharashtra to Kawal face heavy infrastructure throughout their journey. “The corridor is fragmented by open-cast coal mines, the Ada irrigation project, electrified farm fences, and the main Hyderabad-Nagpur railway line,” Siddiqui said. “National Highway 44 acts as the most formidable barrier of all with its heavy traffic and high fencing. It isn’t just one obstacle — it is a cumulative mosaic of risks that forces dispersing tigers to turn back.” He added that while male tigers dispersing from their birthplace are “bolder risk-takers” and can move long distances through human-dominated landscapes, female tigers are more risk-averse and “require quiet, undisturbed habitat to raise cubs.” “Crossing busy highways, railways, and mines poses a massive perceived threat to females,” Siddiqui said. “That is why males occasionally dodge traffic to reach Kawal, but females turn back. Without females, you simply cannot build a breeding population.” Anish Andheria, president and…This article was originally published on Mongabay
body.zh: 印度南部的一个森林老虎保护区栖息着大量的斑点鹿、水鹿、蓝藻羚羊和野猪，这些都是老虎的理想猎物。然而，印度 Mongabay 撰稿人尼维迪卡·克里希南 (Nivedhika Krishnan) 报道称，该保护区没有常驻老虎。特伦甘纳邦的卡瓦尔老虎保护区连接着西部马哈拉施特拉邦塔多巴-安达里保护区和东部恰蒂斯加尔邦因德拉瓦蒂保护区的主要老虎种群。自2015年以来，研究人员证实，只有15只老虎从马哈拉施特拉邦进入卡瓦尔。其中，只有两名是女性。首席研究员伊姆兰·西迪基 (Imran Siddiqui) 告诉 Mongabay India，从马哈拉施特拉邦前往卡瓦尔的老虎在整个旅程中都面临着沉重的基础设施。西迪基说：“这条走廊被露天煤矿、阿达灌溉项目、电气化农场围栏和海得拉巴-那格浦尔主要铁路线分割开来。” “44 号国道交通繁忙，栅栏很高，是所有公路中最可怕的障碍。这不仅仅是一个障碍，而是一系列累积的风险，迫使四散的老虎回头。”他补充说，虽然离开出生地的雄性老虎是“更大胆的冒险家”，可以在人类主导的地区长途跋涉，但雌性老虎则更厌恶风险，“需要安静、不受干扰的栖息地来抚养幼崽”。 “穿越繁忙的高速公路、铁路和矿山对女性构成了巨大的威胁，”西迪基说。 “这就是为什么雄性偶尔会躲避交通到达卡瓦尔，但雌性却会折返。没有雌性，你根本无法建立繁殖种群。” Anish Andheria，总裁……本文最初发表于 Mongabay

reflection.en: The Kawal Tiger Reserve teems with life, a testament to the diverse creation Yahweh has made. Yet, human infrastructure acts as a barrier, preventing the natural order from flourishing fully. It calls us to consider how our development impacts the intricate web of life, and to seek ways to coexist with the wild creatures that share our planet.
reflection.zh: 卡瓦尔老虎保护区生机勃勃，证明了雅伟所造的万物种类繁多。然而，人类的基础设施却成为障碍，阻碍了自然的秩序充分繁荣。这提醒我们思考自身发展如何影响生命的复杂网络，并寻求与共享我们星球的野生动物和谐共处的方式。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: Panama canal traffic to be cut again as drought from El Niño worsens
title.zh: 巴拿马运河因恩尼尼奥干旱加剧而再次限制交通

summary.en: The Panama Canal Authority plans further reductions in daily maritime traffic due to a worsening drought linked to the El Niño climate phenomenon. This will further disrupt one of the world's most critical shipping routes, which handles 5% of global maritime trade and a significant portion of US container traffic.
summary.zh: 巴拿马运河管理局因与厄尔尼诺气候现象相关的干旱加剧而计划进一步减少每日海运交通量。这将进一步扰乱全球最重要的航运路线之一，该航线处理着全球5%的海运贸易和相当一部分美国集装箱运输。

body.en: Latest daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanes The Panama canal plans to again cut maritime traffic due to worsening drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon, further choking up one of the world’s most important shipping lanes. The canal handles 5% of global maritime trade and about 40% of US container traffic; it is favoured by shippers because it usually reduces cost and transit times, especially for companies trading between China, Asia and the US. Continue reading...
body.zh: 最新每日减量将进一步堵塞世界上最重要的航道之一 由于厄尔尼诺气候现象导致干旱加剧，巴拿马运河计划再次削减海上交通，进一步堵塞世界上最重要的航道之一。该运河处理全球5%的海上贸易和美国约40%的集装箱运输；它受到托运人的青睐，因为它通常可以降低成本和运输时间，特别是对于在中国、亚洲和美国之间进行贸易的公司而言。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The drought impacting the Panama Canal is a stark reminder of how natural forces can disrupt global systems, affecting trade and livelihoods. Habakkuk 3:17-18 speaks to finding hope and sustenance in Yahweh even when the natural world seems to fail, and the fig trees do not blossom or the crops fail.
reflection.zh: 巴拿马运河受干旱影响，严峻地提醒我们自然力量如何扰乱全球体系，影响贸易和生计。哈巴谷书3:17-18讲述了即使在自然界似乎枯竭、无花果树不结果、田地没有收成时，也要在雅伟里找到希望和供应。

verse.textEn: Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines... yet I will rejoice in Yahweh.
verse.textZh: 虽然无花果树不发旺，葡萄树不结果……然而，我要因雅伟欢欣。

title.en: EPA eliminates rule that limits planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants
title.zh: 环保局取消限制发电厂温室气体排放的规定

summary.en: The Environmental Protection Agency is repealing rules that limit planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants fueled by coal and natural gas. The agency stated this action would remove over $300 billion in costs for the industry and help "unleash" American energy, marking a significant shift from...
summary.zh: 美国国家环境保护局正在废除限制燃煤和燃气发电厂排放导致地球变暖的温室气体的规定。该机构表示，此举将为该行业节省超过3000亿美元的成本，并有助于“释放”美国能源，这标志着与此前应对气候变化的努力方向发生了根本性转变。

body.en: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Environmental Protection Agency is repealing rules that limit planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants fueled by coal and natural gas, an action the agency said would remove more than $300 billion in costs for the industry and help “unleash” American energy. The rule change, first proposed last year, represents a fundamental shift from efforts by Democratic Presidents Joe Biden and Barack Obama to address climate change and clean up industrial pollution. EPA officials said the change would allow utilities to make the best decisions for their ratepayers rather than be forced to close aging or inefficient plants. By Mathey Daly, Associated Press Banner image: A barge on the Ohio River moves past the Mountaineer Power Plant, a coal-fired power plant near New Haven, W.Va., March 13, 2026. Image courtesy of Carolyn Kaster, Associated PressThis article was originally published on Mongabay
body.zh: 华盛顿（美联社）——美国环境保护局正在废除限制煤炭和天然气发电厂排放导致地球变暖的温室气体的规定，该机构表示，此举将为该行业节省超过 3000 亿美元的成本，并有助于“释放”美国能源。去年首次提出的规则变更代表了民主党总统乔·拜登和巴拉克·奥巴马应对气候变化和清理工业污染的努力的根本转变。美国环保局官员表示，这一变化将使公用事业公司能够为其纳税人做出最佳决策，而不是被迫关闭老化或效率低下的工厂。作者：美联社 Mathey Daly 横幅图片：2026 年 3 月 13 日，俄亥俄河上的一艘驳船驶过西弗吉尼亚州纽黑文附近的 Mountaineer 发电厂。图片由美联社 Carolyn Kaster 提供本文最初发表于 Mongabay

reflection.en: The Earth and all its fullness belong to Yahweh. When regulations designed to protect the environment are rolled back, it raises questions about our role as stewards of creation. The decision to prioritize industrial cost savings over emission limits prompts reflection on how we balance economic needs with our responsibility to care for the planet entrusted...
reflection.zh: 雅伟拥有大地及其万有。当旨在保护环境的法规被撤销时，这引发了关于我们作为受造物管家角色的问题。将工业成本节省置于排放限制之上，促使我们反思如何在平衡经济需求与我们照顾受托之地的责任之间做出选择。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: Iceland, One of Three Countries That Still Hunts Whales, Considers Ban
title.zh: 冰岛，仍捕鲸的三国之一，考虑禁止

summary.en: Iceland is one of only three countries, alongside Norway and Japan, that still permits commercial whaling. However, the Icelandic government is set to introduce a bill in February that could lead to a ban on the practice. This year, Iceland has permitted the hunting of up to 134 minke whales and 150 fin whales by its...
summary.zh: 冰岛是仅有的三个仍允许商业捕鲸的国家之一，与挪威和日本并列。然而，冰岛政府将于二月提出一项可能禁止该做法的法案。今年，冰岛已允许其最后一个捕鲸公司Hvalur捕杀多达134头小须鲸和150头长须鲸。虽然小须鲸并非濒危物种，但长须鲸已被国际自然保护联盟列为易危物种。迄今为止，冰岛已捕杀了80头成年长须鲸，有报道称被鱼叉射...

body.en:
Iceland is one of just three countries, along with Norway and Japan, that still allows commercial whaling in its waters, but that may be about to change. The Icelandic government will put forward a bill in February that could ban the practice.

The Icelandic government will allow for as many as 134 minke whales and 150 fin whales to be killed this year by its last remaining whaling company, Hvalur. While minke whales are not a threatened species, fin whales are classified as vulnerable to extinction by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. So far this year, 80 adult fin whales have been killed in Iceland, where authorities have found that harpooned animals often endure immense suffering. A 2023 report released by the Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority determined that some harpooned whales can take up to two hours to die. The government is now looking to update its whaling law, it says, and will consider a permanent ban on whaling. “This is a really significant milestone in efforts to consign to history Iceland’s cruel and needless whale hunts,” said Wendy Higgins , a spokesperson for Humane World for Animals.

Over the past two decades, Icelandic whalers have killed more than 1,000 fin whales, according to Humane World for Animals, which says that most of the whale meat produced is consumed not by Icelanders but by visiting tourists.

Whaling in the early 20th century decimated populations of cetaceans around the world, leading countries to agree to an international ban on whale hunting in 1986. Despite the ban, Norway resumed commercial whaling in 1993, Iceland in 2006, and Japan in 2019.
body.zh: 冰岛是仅有的三个仍然允许在其水域进行商业捕鲸的国家之一，但这种情况可能即将改变。冰岛政府将于二月份提出一项法案，可能禁止这种做法。 冰岛政府今年将允许其最后一家捕鲸公司 Hvalur 捕杀多达 134 头小须鲸和 150 头长须鲸。虽然小须鲸不是受威胁物种，但长须鲸被国际自然保护联盟列为易危物种。今年到目前为止，冰岛已有 80 头成年长须鲸被杀，当局发现被鱼叉刺伤的动物常常承受巨大的痛苦。冰岛食品和兽医局 2023 年发布的一份报告确定，一些鱼叉鲸可能需要两个小时才能死亡。政府表示，目前正在寻求更新捕鲸法，并将考虑永久禁止捕鲸。人道动物世界发言人温迪·希金斯 (Wendy Higgins) 表示：“这确实是一个重要的里程碑，旨在让冰岛残忍和不必要的鲸鱼捕猎成为历史。” 根据动物人道世界的数据，在过去的二十年里，冰岛捕鲸者已经捕杀了 1000 多头长须鲸，该组织表示，生产的大部分鲸肉不是由冰岛人食用，而是由来访的游客食用。 20 世纪初的捕鲸活动导致世界各地的鲸目动物数量锐减，导致各国于 1986 年同意国际禁止捕鲸。尽管有这项禁令，挪威还是于 1993 年恢复了商业捕鲸，冰岛于 2006 年恢复了商业捕鲸，日本于 2019 年恢复了商业捕鲸。

reflection.en: As Iceland contemplates banning commercial whaling, the plight of the vulnerable fin whale comes into focus. This situation calls to mind the ancient wisdom to "Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for all their rights." The potential ban reflects a growing awareness and a moral imperative to protect species facing extinction....
reflection.zh: 当冰岛考虑禁止商业捕鲸时，易危的长须鲸的困境成为焦点。这一情况让人想起古老的智慧：“为不能说话者说话，为所有被遗弃者伸张正义。” 潜在的禁令反映了日益增长的认识和保护濒危物种的道德责任。 As Iceland contemplates banning commercial whaling, the plight of the vulnerable fin...

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Country diary: Notice anything wrong with this ripe, succulent plum? | Claire Stares
title.zh: 乡村日记：这颗饱满多汁的李子有什么不对劲？

summary.en: Langstone, Hampshire: My garden is full of Victoria plums, but they’re not supposed to be crunchy inside. This summer has been challenging for the fruit trees in my garden, with intense heat and a lack of rain causing poor cropping, premature ripening and pre-harvest drop. While my dessert and cooking apples have...
summary.zh: 兰斯通，汉普郡：我的花园里长满了维多利亚李子，但它们本不该是脆的。今年夏天对花园里的果树来说充满挑战，酷热和缺雨导致收成不佳、过早成熟和采摘前落果。虽然我的食用和烹饪苹果只结了寥寥几颗矮小、像海棠果一样大的果实，榅桲也光秃秃的，但温室旁那棵维多利亚李子树却是个例外。它的枝头挂满了果实，甚至有几根枝条因不堪重负而折断。

body.en: Langstone, Hampshire: My garden is full of Victoria plums, but they’re not supposed to be crunchy inside This summer has been challenging for the fruit trees in my garden, with intense heat and a lack of rain causing poor cropping, premature ripening and pre-harvest drop. While my dessert and cooking apples have produced just a handful of stunted, crab-apple-sized fruit, and my quince is bare, the Victoria plum growing next to the greenhouse is the exception. Its branches are so heavily laden that several have snapped under the weight. Continue reading...
body.zh: 汉普郡兰斯通：我的花园里长满了维多利亚李子，但它们的内部不应该是脆的。今年夏天对我花园里的果树来说是一个挑战，高温和缺乏雨水导致作物歉收、过早成熟和收获前落果。虽然我的甜点和烹饪苹果只结出了一些发育不良、海棠大小的水果，而且我的榅桲也光秃秃的，但生长在温室旁边的维多利亚李是个例外。它的树枝太重了，有几根在重压下折断了。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The intense heat and drought this summer have severely impacted the fruit trees in the author's garden, leading to stunted growth and premature ripening. This mirrors the hardship described in Habakkuk, where even the fig trees and olive trees may fail, and the fields yield no food. Yet, even amidst such scarcity, the passage calls for finding joy in...
reflection.zh: 今年夏天酷热和干旱严重影响了作者花园里的果树，导致生长受阻和过早成熟。这与哈巴谷书中所描述的困境相似，在那里，无花果树和橄榄树可能都会枯干，田地也毫无收成。然而，即使在这种匮乏之中，这段经文仍呼吁在救恩的雅伟上帝里喜乐。

verse.textEn: Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines... yet I will rejoice in Yahweh.
verse.textZh: 虽然无花果树不发旺，葡萄树不结果……然而，我要因雅伟欢欣。

title.en: Rabbits are the biggest threat to Australia’s native species. Why are their numbers booming again?
title.zh: 兔子是澳大利亚本土物种的最大威胁。它们的数量为何又在激增？

summary.en: Scientists attribute the increase in rabbit populations across Australia to favorable rainfall and growing resistance to viruses. A rabbit-detecting dog named Jojo is actively working in South Australia's Bon Bon Reserve, covering significant distances daily to track these animals.
summary.zh: 科学家们将澳大利亚兔子数量的激增归因于有利的降雨和对病毒日益增强的抵抗力。一只名叫乔乔的兔子探测犬正在南澳大利亚邦邦保护区积极工作，每天奔跑很长距离来追踪这些动物。

body.en: Good rainfall and growing resistance to viruses are to blame for growing populations around the country, scientists say Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Jojo the rabbit-detecting dog is working eight days on, two days off, running up to 20km a day chasing rabbits in the south-west of Bon Bon reserve in South Australia’s arid centre. “She’s being kept very busy,” says Dr Pat Taggart, an ecologist with Bush Heritage Australia, a conservation body that owns the former sheep property. Sign up to get climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter Continue reading...
body.zh: 科学家表示，良好的降雨量和对病毒的抵抗力增强是全国兔子数量增加的原因。 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 兔子探测犬 Jojo 正在南澳大利亚干旱中心 Bon Bon 保护区西南部连续工作 8 天，休息两天，每天奔跑 20 公里，追逐兔子。 “她一直很忙，”澳大利亚布什遗产保护机构的生态学家帕特·塔格特博士说，该组织是一个拥有这片前羊财产的保护机构。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The Earth teems with life, a testament to Yahweh's intricate design and wisdom. In Australia, the booming rabbit population, while posing an ecological challenge, is a vivid reminder of the dynamic and sometimes overwhelming abundance of creation. It calls us to consider our role in stewarding this diverse world, recognizing the delicate balance Yahweh has...
reflection.zh: 大地充满生机，证明了雅伟精妙的设计和智慧。在澳大利亚，兔子数量的激增虽然带来了生态挑战，却生动地提醒我们，受造界拥有充满活力且有时令人难以招架的丰盛。这呼吁我们反思在管理这个多元世界中的角色，并认识到雅伟所建立的微妙平衡。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: Artist delights in beautiful ‘mess’ and dead trees of England’s rewilding sites
title.zh: 艺术家乐于英格兰重新野化地点的美丽“混乱”和枯木

summary.en: Artist Rebecca Howard spent two years visiting rewilding projects and painting landscapes for a West Sussex exhibition. While detractors may lament the untidiness, deadwood, and perceived 'mess' of these areas, the exhibition highlights the aesthetic beauty found in fungi growing on dying trees, water buffalo in...
summary.zh: 艺术家丽贝卡·霍华德花了两年时间参观重新野化项目，并为西萨塞克斯郡的一个展览绘制风景画。尽管批评者可能对这些地区的不整洁、枯木和所谓的“混乱”感到惋惜，但该展览突出了在枯树上生长的真菌、湿地里的水牛以及河狸池塘淹没的田野中所发现的美学之美。

body.en: Rebecca Howard spent two years visiting projects and painting landscapes that feature in West Sussex exhibition Rewilding areas do not usually conform to traditional notions of beauty in England’s green and pleasant land. Detractors may bewail the beaver-felled trees, untidy scrub, deadwood, weeds, mud and “mess”. But a new exhibition highlights the aesthetic delights that can be discovered on rewilding sites where fungi grows on dying trees, water buffalo gather in new wetlands and brown-watered beaver pools flood once-desiccated fields. Continue reading...
body.zh: 丽贝卡·霍华德花了两年时间参观西萨塞克斯展览中的项目并绘制风景画。野化地区通常不符合英格兰绿色宜人土地的传统美观念。批评者可能会哀叹被海狸砍伐的树木、杂乱的灌木丛、枯木、杂草、泥土和“混乱”。但一个新的展览强调了在野生动物遗址上可以发现的美学乐趣，那里的真菌在垂死的树木上生长，水牛聚集在新的湿地里，棕色水的河狸池淹没了曾经干涸的土地。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In England's rewilding projects, artist Rebecca Howard sees beauty not in manicured lawns but in the 'mess' of natural processes—dying trees, mud, and untamed growth. This perspective echoes the Genesis account, where Yahweh surveyed all He had made and declared it 'very good.' True beauty often lies beyond our conventional standards, in the vibrant,...
reflection.zh: 在英格兰的重新野化项目中，艺术家丽贝卡·霍华德看到的不是修剪整齐的草坪之美，而是自然过程的“混乱”——枯死的树木、泥泞和未经修饰的生长。这种视角呼应了《创世记》的记载，雅伟审视了祂所造的一切，并宣告“甚好”。真正的美常常超越我们传统的标准，存在于生命本身丰富而复杂的织锦之中。

verse.textEn: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good.
verse.textZh: 神看着一切所造的都甚好。

title.en: The Breakdown of Natural Systems Could Intensify Warming by 30 Percent
title.zh: 自然系统失灵或加剧变暖30%

summary.en: As the planet warms, natural systems like tundras, wetlands, and forests are breaking down, releasing significant emissions that amplify human-caused warming. Research suggests these feedback loops could increase global warming by 20-30%, adding an additional 0.2 degrees Celsius even if net-zero emissions are achieved.
summary.zh: 随着地球变暖，苔原解冻、湿地发酵、森林遭受更大更频繁的野火。这些自然系统的崩溃释放出巨量排放物，进一步加剧了化石燃料燃烧引起的气候变暖。研究表明，这种反馈循环可能将人类引起的气候变暖加剧20%至30%。

body.en:
As the planet heats up, tundras are thawing, wetlands are fermenting, and forests are succumbing to larger and more frequent wildfires. The breakdown of these natural systems is unleashing huge volumes of emissions, further intensifying warming from the burning of fossil fuels. According to new research, such feedback loops could amplify human-driven warming by 20 to 30 percent.

Even if humans reach net zero emissions later this century, feedbacks would add another 0.2 degrees C of warming, according to the modeling study , published this week in Environmental Research Letters. And if the world fails to reach net zero, and countries continue to produce some residual emissions through the end of this century, the added warming would be closer to 0.4 degrees C.

The world is already 1.4 degrees C hotter than in the preindustrial era, and fossil fuel emissions continue to grow, putting the Earth on course to surpass 2.5 degrees C of warming this century, scientists say, well in breach of international climate targets. And yet, while the added warming from feedback loops will further hasten the rise in temperatures, emissions from the breakdown of natural systems are largely absent from the most influential climate models, those that inform climate negotiations.

“This hidden multiplier is missing from the models guiding climate policy, so those models are likely underestimating how much warming is coming — and overestimating how much carbon we can still afford to emit,” said lead author Sam Abernethy, a researcher at Spark Climate Solutions, a San Francisco-based nonprofit that aims to identify climate “blind spots” and account for them in policy. ”To close that gap, we need to understand these processes better and build them into the models we rely on.”

The challenges are steep. Feedback loops are difficult to model, and emissions data is lacking in hard-to-reach places, such as Siberia or the Congo Basin. But as Yale Environment 360 recently reported , scientists around the world are now racing to forecast emissions from natural systems.

“If you’re not including all the emissions going into the atmosphere, you’re hamstrung from the get-go,” Brian Buma, a climate scientist at the Environmental Defense Fund, told e360 . “People are recognizing that the longer we go without taking these emissions into account, there’s just going to be a bigger gap.”
body.zh: 随着地球变暖，苔原正在融化，湿地正在发酵，森林正在遭受更大、更频繁的野火的侵袭。这些自然系统的崩溃正在释放大量的排放物，进一步加剧了化石燃料燃烧造成的变暖。根据新的研究，这种反馈循环可能会将人类导致的变暖幅度放大 20% 至 30%。 根据本周发表在《环境研究快报》上的模型研究，即使人类在本世纪晚些时候达到净零排放，反馈也会使气温再增加 0.2 摄氏度。如果世界未能实现净零排放，并且各国在本世纪末继续产生一些残余排放，则升温幅度将接近 0.4 摄氏度。 科学家表示，世界温度已经比工业化前时代高出 1.4 摄氏度，而化石燃料排放量继续增加，使地球本世纪升温将超过 2.5 摄氏度，这远远违反了国际气候目标。然而，虽然反馈循环带来的额外变暖将进一步加速气温上升，但最有影响力的气候模型（为气候谈判提供信息的模型）基本上不存在自然系统崩溃造成的排放。 “指导气候政策的模型中缺少这个隐藏的乘数，因此这些模型可能低估了即将到来的变暖程度，并高估了我们仍然能够承受的碳排放量，”主要作者萨姆·阿伯内西（Sam Abernethy）说，他是旧金山非营利组织 Spark Climate Solutions 的研究员，旨在识别气候“盲点”并在政策中加以考虑。 “为了缩小这一差距，我们需要更好地理解这些过程，并将它们构建到我们依赖的模型中。” 挑战是严峻的。反馈回路很难建模，西伯利亚或刚果盆地等难以到达的地方缺乏排放数据。但正如耶鲁环境 360 最近报道的那样，世界各地的科学家现在正在竞相预测自然系统的排放量。 美国环境保护基金会的气候科学家布莱恩·布马 (Brian Buma) 告诉 e360：“如果不包括进入大气中的所有排放量，那么从一开始就会受到阻碍。” “人们认识到，不考虑这些排放的时间越长，差距就会越大。”

reflection.en: The prophet Paul speaks of all creation groaning in labor pains, awaiting its ultimate redemption. This news highlights how our planet's natural systems are indeed suffering under the strain of human activity, releasing emissions that worsen the crisis. It calls us to recognize the interconnectedness of all things and our responsibility to care for the...
reflection.zh: 使徒保罗说，万物都在一同劳苦叹息，直到如今，等待着终极的救赎。这则新闻揭示了我们星球的自然系统确实承受着人类活动的重压而痛苦，释放出加剧危机的排放物。这提醒我们认识到万物相互关联，以及我们有责任照管雅伟曾宣告为“甚好”的地球。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Sargassum Superbloom: Seaweed Scourge or Ecological Boon?
title.zh: 马尾藻超级花：海藻灾害还是生态福音？

summary.en: A massive bloom of sargassum seaweed, stretching from West Africa to the Gulf of Mexico, is inundating beaches and harming coastal wildlife. However, scientists have found that this floating algae provides shelter for a wide variety of marine life, leading some to advocate for its protection.
summary.zh: 从西非一直延伸到墨西哥湾的大规模马尾藻爆发，正淹没海滩并杀死沿海野生动物。然而，科学家们发现这种漂浮的海藻为各种海洋生物提供了庇护所，一些人因此呼吁对其进行保护。

body.en:
Stretching from West Africa to the Gulf of Mexico, a massive bloom of sargassum seaweed is swamping beaches and killing coastal wildlife. But scientists have discovered the floating algae also shelters a vast array of ocean creatures, and some are now calling for its protection.

Many of America’s favorite beaches in Florida and the Caribbean have been piled high with foul-smelling seaweed again this summer, often in record amounts. What disappointed tourists may not know is that the inundations, which also smother coral reefs, mangroves, and seagrasses, are just the most visible sign of a vast new marine ecosystem — an expanse of floating sargassum that since 2011 has seemingly come from nowhere to spread in a 5,500-mile-long belt from Mexico to West Africa and Florida to Brazil.

The dense mats of offshore weed grow up to 20 feet thick, and this summer reached a record weight of 38 million metric tons — more than the total weight of all Americans.

The seaweed scourge is wrecking coastal economies in countries heavily dependent on tourism and fishing. The coastlines of 30 countries across the Caribbean and beyond are being visited by the brown mats piling up on beaches, where the weed decomposes, releasing gases such as hydrogen sulfide, with its distinctive rotten-egg smell, and ammonia, which trigger asthma attacks and exacerbate other respiratory conditions. Thousands of victims have been reported by doctors in the Caribbean, especially among workers clearing beaches.

The weed also blocks water intakes and prevents fishers from taking their boats to sea, as well as clogging their nets, engines, and propellers. It has caused mass deaths of marine life on coastlines, while preventing sea turtles from laying their eggs on beaches and blocking hatchlings trying to return to the ocean. The weed also accumulates heavy metals such as arsenic, which leaches out as the weed decomposes on land and can poison water supplies.

Subscribe to the E360 Newsletter for weekly updates delivered to your inbox. Sign Up .

But, while acknowledging its onshore harms, some researchers are now recognizing the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt as a significant new habitat for marine life in the open ocean, and a valuable carbon sink for the planet. According to Jonathan Jung, a marine ecologist at the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry in Mainz, Germany, the weed and its growing army of inhabitants now form “the largest interconnected floating biome on Earth.”

Sargassum seaweed in the Atlantic was once mostly confined to the Sargasso Sea, an area of sluggish waters off Bermuda largely cut off from the rest of the ocean by rotating ocean currents. It has been well-known to mariners since Christopher Columbus reported sailing through “so much grass that it looked like the...
body.zh: 从西非一直延伸到墨西哥湾，大量的马尾藻海藻正在淹没海滩并杀死沿海野生动物。但科学家发现，这些漂浮的藻类也为大量海洋生物提供了庇护，一些海洋生物现在呼吁保护它们。 今年夏天，美国佛罗里达州和加勒比海地区许多最受欢迎的海滩再次堆满了恶臭的海藻，数量往往达到创纪录的水平。失望的游客可能不知道的是，洪水也淹没了珊瑚礁、红树林和海草，而这只是一个巨大的新海洋生态系统最明显的标志——自 2011 年以来，一大片漂浮的马尾藻似乎不知从何而来，在从墨西哥到西非、从佛罗里达到巴西的 5,500 英里长的带上蔓延。 近海杂草丛生，厚度可达 20 英尺，今年夏天的重量达到创纪录的 3800 万吨——超过了所有美国人的总重量。 海藻祸害正在破坏严重依赖旅游业和渔业的国家的沿海经济。加勒比海及其他地区30个国家的海岸线正被堆积在海滩上的棕色垫子所覆盖，这些杂草在海滩上分解，释放出硫化氢等气体，具有独特的臭鸡蛋味，还有氨气，会引发哮喘发作并加剧其他呼吸道疾病。加勒比地区的医生报告了数千人的受害者，特别是清理海滩的工人。 这种杂草还会阻塞进水口，阻止渔民将船出海，并堵塞渔网、发动机和螺旋桨。它导致海岸线海洋生物大量死亡，同时阻止海龟在海滩上产卵，并阻止试图返回海洋的幼龟。这种杂草还会积累砷等重金属，当杂草在陆地上分解时，砷会渗出，污染水源。 订阅 E360 新闻通讯，每周更新发送到您的收件箱。报名 。 但是，在承认其陆上危害的同时，一些研究人员现在认识到大大西洋马尾藻带是公海海洋生物的重要新栖息地，也是地球宝贵的碳汇。德国美因茨马克斯·普朗克化学研究所的海洋生态学家乔纳森·荣格表示，这种杂草及其不断增长的居民大军现在形成了“地球上最大的相互关联的漂浮生物群落”。 大西洋中的马尾藻海藻曾经主要局限于马尾藻海，这是百慕大附近的一个缓慢水域，由于旋转洋流，基本上与海洋其他部分隔绝。自从克里斯托弗·哥伦布报道航行穿过“如此多的草，看起来就像……”以来，它就为水手们所熟知。

reflection.en: The vastness of the sargassum bloom, stretching across oceans, reveals the intricate and often surprising ways Yahweh sustains life. Even in what appears to be a nuisance, a hidden ecosystem thrives, showcasing the Creator's abundant wisdom in every corner of the earth.
reflection.zh: 马尾藻的巨大爆发，横跨海洋，揭示了雅伟维持生命的复杂而令人惊讶的方式。即使在看似令人烦恼的事物中，一个隐藏的生态系统也在蓬勃发展，展示了造物主在地上每个角落里丰富的智慧。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: Chinese Industry Is Starting to Wean Off Fossil Fuels
title.zh: 中国工业开始摆脱化石燃料

summary.en: By several measures, Chinese industry is becoming less dependent on fossil fuels, according to a new analysis. New clean power generation exceeded the growth in demand last year, leading to a decrease in coal output, with eight provinces showing declines in coal generation and nine others seeing slower growth.
summary.zh: 根据一项新分析，中国工业在多项指标上正日益摆脱对化石燃料的依赖。去年，新增清洁能源发电量超过了需求增长，导致煤炭产量下降，其中八个省份的煤炭发电量出现下降，另外九个省份的煤炭发电量增长则显著放缓。

body.en:
By several measures, Chinese industry is becoming less dependent on fossil fuels, according to a new analysis.

New clean power more than met the growth in demand across China last year, leading to a small decline in coal output, according to think tank Ember. Analysts identified eight provinces where coal generation is now seeing declines, including industrial centers such as Hunan and Shandong, and it named another nine provinces where the growth of coal generation has slowed substantially.

On top of declines in coal power, factories are moving away from using fossil fuels for industrial processes. Textile plants may use gas boilers to generate heat for dyeing fabrics, for instance, while food producers may use gas ovens for cooking. But increasingly such processes are being electrified.

In eight of 11 industrial sectors — including textiles, food, pharmaceuticals, and machinery — fossil fuel use has already peaked, the analysis found. The declines come even as China’s industrial output continues to grow.

“The clean electricity system is gaining both strength and scope, and the fossil fuel system is already registering the shift,” said Muyi Yang, a senior analyst at Ember. “You can see fossil fuel use flattening out, sector by sector and province by province.”
body.zh: 一项新的分析显示，通过多项措施，中国工业对化石燃料的依赖正在减少。 据智库 Ember 称，去年新增的清洁能源远远满足了中国各地的需求增长，导致煤炭产量小幅下降。分析师确定了煤炭发电量目前出现下降的八个省份，其中包括湖南和山东等工业中心，并指出了另外九个煤炭发电量增长大幅放缓的省份。 除了煤炭发电量下降之外，工厂正在逐渐不再使用化石燃料进行工业生产。例如，纺织厂可能使用燃气锅炉产生热量来染色织物，而食品生产商可能使用燃气烤箱进行烹饪。但此类过程正在日益电气化。 分析发现，在 11 个工业部门中，有 8 个部门——包括纺织、食品、制药和机械——化石燃料的使用已经达到顶峰。尽管中国的工业产出持续增长，但经济仍出现下滑。 Ember 高级分析师 Muyi Yang 表示：“清洁电力系统的强度和范围都在增强，而化石燃料系统也已经发生了这种转变。” “你可以看到化石燃料的使用逐个部门、逐个省份趋于平缓。”

reflection.en: The news that China's industry is reducing its reliance on fossil fuels is a hopeful sign. It echoes the wonder of creation, where diverse systems work together, as Psalm 104:24 reminds us: "How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures."
reflection.zh: 中国工业正减少对化石燃料依赖的消息，是一个令人鼓舞的迹象。这呼应了受造界的奇妙，其中各种系统协同运作，正如诗篇 104:24 所提醒我们的：“雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你智慧的作为；全地充满了你的创造物。”

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。
